 Dated this the 24th day of June, 2025  JUDGMENT

The writ petition is filed with the following prayers;
"i. Quash Exhibit-P7 and allow the petitioner to continue the Street vending activity.
II. Issue a writ of mandamus or other appropriate writ or order directing the Respondents 1 to 5 not to evict the writ petitioner nor prevent the writ petitioner from carry on his livelihood of street vending activity in front of the District Court Complex, Thalassery beside the centenary park Thalassery.
III. Remove all obstructions caused by Respondents 1 to 5 in conducting the street vending activity opposite to the district court Thalassery which was being conducted on regular basis at the location.

Navas T vs The Tahsildar (Lr) -Thalassery on 24 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169201334/
2 IV.
Grant such other reliefs as this Hon'ble court may deem, fit and proper in the circumstances of the case.

"
2. This Court, upon admission of the writ petition, passed the following order on 24.01.2025;
"The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the Municipality submits that the petitioner himself has vacated the premises, which is subject matter of the present writ petition.
The learned Standing Counsel has also shown me the video of the petitioner shifting the premises himself.

2. Taking into consideration the submission of the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent Municipality, I am of the view that the petitioner is not entitled to any interim order in the present writ petition.
3. The learned Government Pleader and the learned Standing Counsel for the respondent Municipality shall file their counter affidavits within a period of two weeks.

The counter affidavit on behalf of the government states that the petitioner had encroached upon Government land, and on noticing the same, he was given a notice on 21.12.2015 requiring him to vacate the land.

The petitioner then filed O.S No.06 of 2016 on the files of the Munsiff Court,
Thalassery and obtained an interim injunction restraining the removal of the petty shop otherwise than by the due process of law.

In accordance with the said order, the village Officer Thalassery submitted A Form report under the provisions of the Kerala Land Conservancy Act, and thereafter,
the Tahsildar (LR) issued a B Form notice on 23.07.2016.
The petitioner did not participate in the enquiry.
4. A second notice was issued on 10.08.2016.
After a due enquiry, the Tahsildar had passed an order on 30.07.2019 directing the petitioner to vacate the land within 15 days.

On receipt of the same, the petitioner filed WP(C) No.22480 of 2019 before this Court, which was disposed of on 02.12.2019,
directing the petitioner to invoke the statutory remedies.

Thereafter, the petitioner filed an application before the Sub Collector, Thalassery, as per the provisions of the Street Vendors Act instead of filing any appeal against the order of the Tahsildar (LR) referred to above, under the provisions of the Kerala Land Conservancy Act and Rules, which has become final.
2025:KER:45569 WP(C) NO.2874 OF 2025 5.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner thereafter filed WP(C) No.27543 of 2020, which was disposed of, recording the submission of the Standing Counsel for the Thalassery Municipality that a street vending licence was granted to the petitioner.
6. The petitioner had also filed case No.24 of 2020 before the Grievance Committee constituted under Section 20 of the Act for redressal of the grievance of street vendors.

"In the result, we grant injunction against the respondents from preventing the petitioner to do vending of Fast Food, Tea etc in the mobile cart which vehicle he can keep lay the side of the public road and that too after complying with Kovid-19 Protocols.
But this order is not giving permission to the petitioner to use any portions of the puramboke land for his vending.
The Revenue authorities can prevent him from encroaching on the puramboke land for vending except for keeping his mobile vending cart from which the petitioner can vend.

The Revenue and Municipal authorities is directed to obey this order in view of the permissions in the Central Act.No.07/2014."
7.
The above clearly shows that the petitioner could not have encroached upon the Government land, and the petitioner and the Municipality were bound by the final order dated 29 th April 2021.
Again, a notice was issued to the petitioner to vacate the encroachment, and the entire area was vacated, and the petitioner was removed on 13.01.2025 from the Government land.
8. The prayer is as such in the writ petition became infructuous.

However, as contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that he still holds a licence under the Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014, as seen from Ext.P6 dated 25.09.2024, which is valid till 24.09.2026, it will be open to the petitioner to request respondent No.4 to specify the place wherein he can carry on the business, for which Ext.P6 licence has been granted.

entities.text: Street Vendors (Protection of Livelihood and Regulation of Street Vending) Act, 2014
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Orders shall be passed by the 4th respondent as directed above within three weeks from the date of receipt of an appropriate application from the petitioner in that regard.
The writ petition is disposed of as above.
